nodes.summary: Every group $G$, finite or infinite, whose set of element orders $\{\operatorname{ord}(g) : g \in G\}$ equals $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 7\}$ is isomorphic to $L_2(7) = \mathrm{PSL}(2, 7)$, the projective special linear group of $2 \times 2$ matrices over the field $\mathbb{Z}/7\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: Lytkina–Kuznetsov theorem: PSL(2, 7) is recognizable by spectrum

nodes.summary: The statement that every group $G$, finite or infinite, whose set of element orders $\{\operatorname{ord}(g) : g \in G\}$ equals $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 7\}$ is isomorphic to $L_2(7) = \mathrm{PSL}(2, 7)$, the projective special linear group of $2 \times 2$ matrices over the field $\mathbb{Z}/7\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 16.57: recognition of PSL(2, 7) by spectrum
